meta.title: Theranos: The $9 Billion Illusion — Reel 3
meta.topic: The rise and fall of Theranos and Elizabeth Holmes
meta.description: How a Stanford dropout built a nine billion dollar company on a lie that endangered real patients' lives. The full story of Theranos, Elizabeth Holmes, and the fraud that changed Silicon Valley.

lines.text: The Edison was physically, biologically, and mathematically incapable of doing what Holmes promised.
To hide the failure, Theranos resorted to massive, coordinated fraud across their entire operation.
They secretly bought commercial Siemens blood analyzers and hid them in a separate basement lab.
Employees were ordered to hack the Siemens machines open to accommodate the tiny, diluted patient samples.
Because the blood was artificially diluted, the results were highly erratic and statistically invalid.
Real patients were receiving terrifyingly false medical diagnostics, from fake H.I.V. results to false cancer markers.
The facade cracked when young whistleblowers like Tyler Shultz and Erika Cheung realized what was happening.
They noticed that quality control data was being routinely manipulated or deleted to pass inspections.
When they reported it to management, they were threatened with massive corporate lawsuits and intimidation tactics.
But the secret reached Wall Street Journal reporter John Carreyrou, who began a quiet, relentless investigation.
Despite Holmes deploying elite lawyers to kill the story, Carreyrou published the devastating expose in 2015.
The article destroyed the illusion instantly. Medical agencies raided the labs and banned Holmes from operating.
